items.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006
items.q: Paul Parker was here when I was a student. He was a professor but he played some but not a great deal.

ctx.x: What’s the connection between the Catatonic Five and the Fallacious Five? Was that a little bit before?

That was before. And I think Emerson and Donny perhaps were the — that was, you know Paul Parker was here when I was a student. He was a professor but he played some but not a great deal. But that was a little before. And you stand on the shoulders of giants. That’s what got it all started. And then we just came at the right time. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

Isn’t it interesting, at least I feel in those times, when you’re 18 and someone’s 21 back in those times, and they have more experience, they just seem so much older and wiser and everything. Then you get older and three years is almost nothing.
